LipidOracle
Install Workflow ID levels Outputs Reference

Lipid annotation from MS1 and MS2 data.

Annotation engine for CID, EAD, and UVPD spectra, with C=C position and oxidation calls in acyl chains. Runs as a Docker container.

Install Read the paper

Every run writes a self-contained dashboard.html next to the CSVs. No server, no upload.

Two commands to a first run

LipidOracle ships as a Docker image. Put your .mgf file in a local input folder and mount it alongside an output folder.

Pull the image from Docker Hub.

docker pull zambonilab/lipidoracle

Mount your folders and run. MS2 data, and optionally MS1, come from a single .mgf file.

docker run --rm \
  -v <INPUT-FOLDER>:/input \
  -v <OUTPUT-FOLDER>:/output \
  zambonilab/lipidoracle

Review the parameters, then run again. On the first run, if no lipidoracle.yaml is found in either folder, LipidOracle writes a default one to the output folder and stops so you can check it.

WORKFLOW:
  lipidoracle: True       # internal MS1/MS2 annotation engine
  acyl_analysis: False    # EAD/UVPD analysis of acyl chains
  rt_check: liri          # False | legacy | liri | hydra

What happens on a run

Each stage narrows the candidate set and raises the identification level of the matches it produces.

Load spectra

Reads MS2 and MS1 from the MGF. An m/z target list and internal standards can be pinned in.

input

Build libraries

Internal LipidOracle library, optionally LipiDex, LipidBlast, and your own CSV libraries.

setup

Match on accurate mass

Identifies features by precursor m/z against every library in play.

idlevel 1

Match on MS2

Every idlevel 1 hit that carries MS2 goes on to fragment matching and scoring.

idlevel 2

Validate retention time

A class-specific model flags implausible hits. External RT anchors refine the fit.

filter

Resolve acyl chains

On EAD or UVPD spectra, locates C=C and oxidation positions by scoring simulated isomer spectra.

idlevel 3

Consolidate and export

Aggregates isomer candidates per spectrum, then writes results, diagnostics, and the dashboard.

idlevel 4

Every row carries its evidence

Identification levels say what a call is actually based on, so you can filter the output to the confidence your work needs.

1

Accurate mass

Matched on m/z alone. MS2 fields are usually empty on these rows.

2

MS2 match

Ranked by score_L2, a hybrid of how well the weighted library spectrum was matched and how well the spectra correlate. A modified cosine score is reported alongside it for information.

3

Double-bond position

The feature was analysed for C=C and oxidation position in its acyl chains. score_L3 compares simulated isomer spectra, with separate scoring for lipids and for oxidised PUFAs.

4

Consolidated call

One row per spectrum, aggregating the idlevel 3 candidates.

Pick how strict retention time gets

WORKFLOW.rt_check selects exactly one plausibility engine, applied after MS1 and MS2 matching.

Default liri

Builds a retention index and fits a monotone map to RT independently for each class and ether group, using only that group's own anchors. It is never wrong for lack of evidence, but it stays silent on classes with too few anchors, so it will not filter MS1-only hits for rare classes such as FAs and CEs.

hydra

Shares one calibration curve across classes through a chemistry-informed feature vector. It can flag implausible hits in classes with no anchors of their own, and is more aggressive on idlevel 1.

legacy

The two linear regressions ported from the Python codebase. Kept for rollback and comparison. Measured removal precision is close to a coin flip.

False

Disables retention time checking entirely.

What lands in the output folder

Two files answer most questions. The rest of the run is written to diag/ so you can trace any call back to its evidence.

Results

  • annotation.csv
  • summary.csv
  • annotation_full.csv
  • summary_by_feature.csv

Diagnostics

  • input_spectra.csv
  • annotation_idlevel1.csv

Reference

LipidOracle is developed by the Zamboni lab at ETH Zurich. Version 1.0 is a full rewrite in Rust. The Python version stays available as zambonilab/lipidoracle:v0.9, and is not backward compatible.

Wu et al. Optimisation of electron-induced dissociation parameters for molecular annotation of glycerides and phospholipids in fast LC-MS Analyst, 2025. 10.1039/d5an00567a
